chapter: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
title: Mildred's arrangers, King of Jazz and the Old Gold broadcasts
summary: Bill Challis, Lenny Hayton and William Grant Still wrote for her; the band was paid while Whiteman made King of Jazz, and Norvo, in Minneapolis, fell for her voice on the radio.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Fancy that. What'd he do, put an arranger to work to make her arrangements?
Huh?
Did you say he had an arranger to work on her --
Oh, yes.
Who was doing them, I mean outside --
Well I think the two arrangers, I think Bill Challis --
Yeah.
-- and course there was Lenny Hayton --
YEAH. Right, right.
And William Grant Still did a lot of things for her, because they had voices later -- they had voices behind her a lot of the times --
Yeah, yeah.
-- spirituals --
When did -- when did the -- when did they identify her as the 'Rocking Chair' lady? That was a little later I think, wasn't it?
Oh, I don't know, Hoagy was out there with the band all that time --
Yeah.
And she used to think, -- sing --
I guess I just made a guess --
Well Hoagy had -- yeah she used to sing Hoagy's songs. He used to hang out with the Whiteman band.
Yeah.
And -- an opinion here and there about, why it was is not important but that except it's been a good
deal, the Whiteman spent a great deal of time making 'King of Jazz' --
Yeah.
-- and they were -- they got paid every week, regardless.
Oh --
-- whether they worked or didn't work --
Yeah --
-- they worked for the sets, and so every week they went and picked up their checks.
Yeah, yeah, that was something, wasn't it?
So all Mildred did was the Old Gold program, which was every Thursday night, because I was in Minneapolis by this time and I used to listen, it just killed me the first time I heard it --
Yeah.
-- I guess I was in love with her before I ever knew her.
